one_line: Anthropic's IPO fuels multibillion funding as AI tools, hardware, and regulation intensify.

themes.title: Anthropic IPO attracts multibillion funding
themes.text: Anthropic set an IPO price of $70‑$78 per share, valuing the company up to $1.404 trillion and aiming to raise up to $64 billion from the public offering. Nvidia pledged $10 billion and TSMC approved up to $500 million in shares, while co‑founders will sell $1.75 billion of stock.

stories.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price at $70–$78 per share, targeting $1.4 trillion valuation
Anthropic co-founders to sell $1.75 billion in shares ahead of $1.4 trillion IPO
Nvidia plans $10B investment in Anthropic alongside its IPO
TSMC to invest up to $1B in Anthropic and OpenAI at IPO price

themes.title: Anthropic expands tools and performance
themes.text: Anthropic launched Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, and Data for collaborative use, and its Fable 5.2 model achieved 41.3% of freelance jobs on the Remote Labor Index, far ahead of competitors.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, and Data
Fable 5.2 tops Remote Labor Index at 41.3% of freelance jobs

themes.title: Google rolls out new AI hardware
themes.text: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon publicly available with a swarm‑agent feature and introduced TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max chips designed for confidential and large‑scale AI workloads.

stories.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Carbon to the public with agent swarm feature
Google unveils TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max for confidential and large-scale AI workloads

themes.title: Regulators tighten AI chip oversight
themes.text: New York opened a registration portal for large AI developers under the RAISE Act, while a Singapore‑based network was linked to evading U.S. export controls on Nvidia chips and a reported affair involving Jensen Huang has raised the likelihood of U.S. chip export limits in the NDAA.

stories.headline: Nvidia spy scandal exposes Singapore chip networks evading US export controls
New York launches portal for AI safety law requiring developer registration
Jensen Huang affair raises chances of US chip export limits in NDAA
